content: August 2026: the memory subsystem underwent a major architectural overhaul, introducing Phase 1–17 of episodic memory consolidation, valence scoring, and cross-store interlinking with knowledge and experience systems.
August 2026: the Working Memory Cortex framework was fully implemented as a dedicated module, enabling real-time live-streaming of working-memory snapshots via the WMC Studio SPA.
August 2026: job hunt workflows were refactored into modular aurora primitives, with Layer 0 runtime, Layer 2 config spec, and shared graph registry for cross-service deduplication.
August 2026: Threads service gained full multimodal support—image description parsing, link previewing, and memory-persistent reply logging for enhanced social interaction.
August 2026: Spec Studio was layered into five distinct components (Layers 0–4), with a DAG-based UI shell and per-user episodic memory storage for targeted cognitive visualization.
August 2026: the cognition framework was expanded with metacognitive context checkpoints, grounded awareness signals, and adaptive speech rate control for real-time user feedback parsing.
August 2026: unified tool-result caching was introduced as a first-class DAG step, enabling resilient agentic workflows with per-identity working-memory publishing via live-state Grasp hub.
August 2026: episodic memory distillation (EMC-4 → SM) and EMC-6 grouping were wired into the flush_staging pipeline, with episode-layer UI and provenance tracking for cognitive lineage.
August 2026: email-based job searching was enabled in the graph engine, with server-side folder filtering for ProtonMail and concurrent RSS processing for raw message tracking.
August 2026: comprehensive tool definitions were consolidated into `needle-tools.json`, standardizing job hunt toolkit configurations and cross-service workflow dependencies.
